messages:
caroline-sales: Heads up — BigBank POC confirmed traffic profile. Steady ~180 RPS (95th) but they have short spikes to ~500–700 RPS for ~30s every ~2–3 hours. They want an enterprise reserve + burst plan. Need sizing + pricing + security checklist answers by EOD.
josh-solutions: Quick Q — are those spikes many parallel short requests (chat-style) or a few long prompts? Makes a big diff for batching/kv cache.
anya-sre: They said mix. ~85% short chats (~20–60 tokens) and ~15% long completions up to 2k tokens. KV/prefix warmup matters.
ram-runtime: Back-of-envelope: steady 180 RPS * avg 40 tokens ≈ 7.2k tokens/s. Burst 700 RPS ≈ 28k tokens/s. For LLMs we usually recommend reserved pool equivalent to 4 GPUs for steady + 4–8 GPUs in burst pool depending on model. If we use quantized variants during bursts we can cut GPU need ~30–50%.
kai-security: Security flag — BigBank requires PCI scope minimization + SOC2. They want KMS integration + VPC-only control plane. Also need data retention & deletion notes for the questionnaire.
caroline-sales: Pricing ask from the customer: ballpark monthly cost for reserved pool + 10% burst credit cushion. I need a number to put in the proposal.
ram-runtime: Draft autoscale policy (proposal):
```yaml
autoscale:
  min_replicas: 4            # reserved capacity for steady traffic
  target_rps_per_replica: 50
  max_replicas: 14           # allows burst up to ~700 RPS
  burst_policy:
    enabled: true
    burst_pool_gpus: 4       # separate burst reserve we can bill as credits
    quantized_fallback: true # use 4-bit quantized variant under heavy load
  cooldown_seconds: 30
```
This maps to: reserve 4 GPUs, burst pool 4 GPUs (hot), autoscale up to 14 replicas total if needed. Exact mapping depends on model throughput profile.
infra-bot: Cost-sim run complete — estimate: $72,300/mo reserve (4x high-memory GPUs) + ~$9,400/mo expected burst credits (based on 3 short spikes/day). Margin = +20% ops buffer. Link: https://ops.redwood.example/sim/6823456789
anya-sre: Operational notes: prewarm KV cache for common prefixes 60s before expected spike windows. Prefer quantized model variant for burst handling. Add canary fallback to smaller model if tail latency > 1s.
josh-solutions: I'll draft the proposal with two options: (A) conservative: reserve 4 GPUs + burst pool 4 (higher cost, lower risk), (B) cost-optimized: reserve 2 GPUs + larger burst + stricter fallback to 4-bit quant model. @ram-runtime can you validate per-model perf numbers for both?
ram-runtime: Will run model bench matrix and post numbers by 15:00 UTC. Also include end-to-end p99 tail latency estimates for each config.
kai-security: I'll answer the questionnaire items re: KMS, data flows, and deployment isolation. Expect a signed doc by 16:00 UTC.
caroline-sales: Perfect. If we get final numbers + security answer by 15:30 UTC I can send the proposal and aim to close the commit today. Thanks team :pray:
